title: Sunny Hears the Rain | Bedtime Story
description: When the rain begins to fall in the Australian bush, Sunny the quokka snuggles under a giant fern leaf and listens to the most beautiful lullaby in the world. A hushed, cosy story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories for little ones who love rainy nights.
narration:
The sky had been getting heavier all afternoon, full and grey and soft.

Sunny was out in the bush when the first drop fell. It landed on a broad green leaf with a soft little tap.

Then another drop. And another.

The rain was beginning.

Sunny looked around. Just nearby was the most enormous fern she had ever seen, its long wide leaves spread out like a roof. She trotted over and tucked herself underneath.

She was perfectly dry. And perfectly cosy.

From her little shelter, she listened.

The rain fell on the big fern leaves above her — a soft, steady drumming, like tiny fingers pattering on a table.

It fell on the thin papery bark of the gum tree nearby — a dry, crispy whisper.

It fell on the moss-covered rocks — a deep, slow drip, drip, drip.

It fell in the puddles — a bubbly little pop with each drop.

Every surface had its own sound. Every leaf, every rock, every patch of earth was playing a different part of the same song.

Sunny closed her eyes and let the music wash over her.

The rain grew softer. And softer still. The bush smelled clean and sweet and green, the way it only ever smells when it rains.

Sunny curled up tighter, her nose tucked against her paws. The rain pattered on, gentle and steady and kind.

It sang her slowly all the way to sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, rain. Goodnight, little one.
